change.title: pr-3-flat
change.description: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Substring match upsamples negated and mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. On the discover dataset, with all projects allowlisted, those queries get `count()` rewritten to `upsampled_count()` = `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Transactions don't have a sample weight, so the chart shows a wrong count and nothing tells the user. Parse the query (for example with `event_search.parse_search_query`) and only return True for a positive `event.type:error` filter that is not negated and not inside an OR. Add a test for `!event.type:error`.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink `sentry-repo` (Subproject commit a5d29095…), and the repository has no `.gitmodules` entry for it. It looks like a nested checkout that got committed by accident. It breaks `git submodule` operations and clones, and has nothing to do with the feature. Remove it from the index.

findings.title: Cache adds 60s staleness for a cheap option read; invalidation helper is never called
findings.body: The cache wraps one `options.get` and a membership check, which costs no more than the cache round-trip that replaces it. After an allowlist change, results stay stale for up to 60s. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) has no caller anywhere in the repository, so the consistency its docstring promises never happens. The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` (lines 50-53) says the allowlist is read "fresh each time", which this cache contradicts. Consider dropping the cache and the dead helper, or wiring the invalidation into the option change. Also note that the allowlist check is O(n·m) over a list; a `set(allowlist)` would avoid that.

findings.title: Eligibility uses the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but the check passes the closed-over request `dataset`. In the dashboard-split paths (lines 362-452), queries run against `discover` while `dataset` is a metrics dataset. For those, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False, and the errors part of a split widget is never upsampled even when the same chart elsewhere is. If those queries should be upsampled, pass `scoped_dataset`.

findings.title: Same transform repeated in three branches with misleading comments
findings.body: `final_columns` is computed the same way in all three branches (lines 232-233, 276-277, 295-296), and `should_upsample` is copied into `upsampling_enabled` for no reason. Comments such as "late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions" and "allows for better query optimization and caching" don't describe what the code does. Compute `final_columns` once right after the eligibility check.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` declares result type `number` but returns toInt64
findings.body: The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64`, and `count()` declares `integer`. Declaring `number` changes the field meta the frontend uses to format the replaced `count` series. Use `default_result_type="integer"`.

findings.title: Direct model creation instead of factory helper
findings.body: CLAUDE.md (Common Gotchas #7) says to use `self.create_*` helpers rather than direct model creation. Use `self.create_organization(name="test-org")` instead of `Organization.objects.create`.

findings.title: Comment contradicts assertion; no coverage for negated/mixed queries
findings.body: The comments say "First bucket has 1 event", but the assertion expects 10, which is the upsampled value. Say that explicitly. None of the endpoint tests covers `!event.type:error` or OR queries on discover, which is where the substring check misfires.

findings.title: Broad exception swallowing and falsy check in sample_rate helper
findings.body: `except Exception: pass` hides a malformed `contexts` in test data. `if client_sample_rate:` silently skips a rate of `0`. Use `isinstance` checks on the dicts and `is not None` so that fixture mistakes show up.

contracts.action: Endpoint decides whether to upsample via is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects
contracts.equivalent_path: Dataset selection at organization_events_stats.py:170-189 and dashboard split at 359-452 choose scoped_dataset per query
contracts.before_after: The split paths pass discover as scoped_dataset, but the new check reads the outer request dataset, so the decision can differ from the dataset actually queried
contracts.visible_effect: count() series is replaced by sum(sample_weight) aliased count in the stats response
contracts.failure_mode: Substring match in _is_error_focused_query upsamples negated/mixed discover queries, giving wrong counts with no error; a cache miss/hit only adds staleness

contracts.action: New SnQL function upsampled_count resolved via 'upsampled_count() as count'
contracts.equivalent_path: count() in DiscoverDatasetConfig; ErrorsQueryBuilder extends DiscoverQueryBuilder so it uses the same config
contracts.before_after: Alias syntax is accepted by FUNCTION_PATTERN, so the result key stays 'count'
contracts.visible_effect: Same series key, with the value multiplied by the sample weight
contracts.failure_mode: If sample_weight is null (transactions), sum returns 0/null, so the count is silently wrong

summary: The PR rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) when every queried project is on the allowlist. Two things should be fixed. First, the check for error queries is a plain substring match, so `!event.type:error` and OR queries on discover also get upsampled and show wrong counts. Second, a stray `sentry-repo` submodule gitlink was committed. The rest are suggestions: the 60s cache gains little and its invalidation helper is never called, the eligibility check reads the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried, the transform is repeated in three branches, `upsampled_count` declares the wrong result type, and there are small test and rule nits.
